name: compiler_correct
prelude:
inductive Expr where
  | lit : Nat → Expr
  | add : Expr → Expr → Expr
inductive Instr where
  | push : Nat → Instr
  | plus : Instr
def eval : Expr → Nat
  | .lit n => n
  | .add l r => eval l + eval r
def compile : Expr → List Instr
  | .lit n => [.push n]
  | .add l r => compile l ++ compile r ++ [.plus]
def run : List Instr → List Nat → Option (List Nat)
  | [], s => some s
  | .push n :: code, s => run code (n :: s)
  | .plus :: code, a :: b :: s => run code ((b + a) :: s)
  | .plus :: _, _ => none
statement: theorem compiler_correct (e : Expr) : run (compile e) [] = some [eval e]
proofs:
have continuation (t : Expr) (code : List Instr) (s : List Nat) :
      run (compile t ++ code) s = run code (eval t :: s) := by
    induction t generalizing code s with
    | lit n => rfl
    | add l r il ir =>
      simp only [compile, List.append_assoc, il, ir, List.cons_append, List.nil_append, run, eval]
  simpa [run] using continuation e [] []
  have append_run (as bs : List Instr) (s : List Nat) :
      run (as ++ bs) s = (run as s).bind (run bs) := by
    induction as generalizing s with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons a as ih =>
      cases a with
      | push n => simpa [run] using ih (n :: s)
      | plus =>
        cases s with
        | nil => rfl
        | cons a s => cases s with
          | nil => rfl
          | cons b s => simpa [run] using ih ((b + a) :: s)
  have stack (t : Expr) (s : List Nat) : run (compile t) s = some (eval t :: s) := by
    induction t generalizing s with
    | lit n => rfl
    | add l r il ir => simp [compile, append_run, il, ir, run, eval]
  exact stack e []
strategies: Induct on expressions with both continuation code and stack generalized.
Prove execution composition for arbitrary programs, then establish a stack invariant.
